Local symbols: $D_i(b,l)$ is the minimum flip count after processing $i$ mask entries, ending with bit
$b$ and capped run length $l$; $m_b$ is its required run length (counts). Bits and $\mathrm{cost}_i(b)$, the
candidate flip cost at position $i$, are dimensionless.
$\mathsf H$ is the dimensionless reflection matrix, distinct from the Riemann eigenvector matrix $\mathsf R$.
These symbols are proposed in the notation issue.

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What it does.** A static Boolean mask marks solid cells. Rectification repairs runs that are too thin by
flipping fluid cells to solid along each line; during a stage the face states at a fluid-solid interface are
mirrored, the solid cells carry placeholder primitives, the implicit system gets a reflecting closure at
every fluid-solid face and an identity row in every solid cell, and the solid conserved cells are refilled
after each RK combination.

**Switch.** `vars["solid"]` supplied at initialization; `boundary-condition/internal/max-iter` (default 5),
`solid-density` ($10^3\ \mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$) and `solid-pressure` ($10^9\ \mathrm{Pa}$).

**Requires / implies / turns off.** The implicit solve requires both x1 faces physical (no x1 decomposition).
Solid cells are excluded from the gravity-work fixer's mass and get a sound speed of
$10^{-8}\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ in the time-step bound.

**Order.** The line optimum of the flips is exact; the closure is exact; the geometry is a cell-aligned
staircase with no measured convergence order.

**Defining equation.** @eq-ch11-solids-dp and @eq-ch11-solids-closure.
:::

An immersed solid is a set of cells, not a surface: the mask says which cells are solid, and the solver
closes every face between a fluid cell and a solid cell as if it were a reflecting wall. Two things make
that work. The mask must not contain runs that are thinner than the reconstruction stencil can close, which
is what the rectification guarantees along every grid line; and the solid cells must hold a state the
reconstruction and the implicit solve can read without producing a flux, which is what the placeholder fill,
the face mirror and the masked rows provide.

### Derivation

At a single fluid-solid interface, copy the fluid reconstructed state to the solid side and negate its normal
velocity. This yields the reflecting pair derived in @sec-ch11-reflecting, now at a face of a staircase mask.
`InternalBoundaryImpl::forward` ({{< code src/bc/internal_boundary.cpp InternalBoundaryImpl::forward >}})
applies that rule after the fluid side has been reconstructed: for every row the solid-side face state
takes the fluid-side value, and the normal velocity row of the direction being swept takes its negative. A
face with solid on both sides has no fluid flux interpretation in this argument.

The rectification problem on one line minimizes the count of changed zeros. Set $m_0=3$ and $m_1=2$.
A candidate equal to the original bit costs zero; changing zero to one costs one; changing one to zero has
infinite cost. Start with $D_0(0,0)=D_0(1,0)=0$ and all other states infinite. Extending the current bit increments
its run length, capped at $m_b$. Switching to the other bit starts length one only if the previous length is
zero (the start) or at least $m_b$. For every permitted predecessor, update the candidate state by the minimum
of its existing cost and predecessor cost plus the flip cost:

$$
D_{i+1}(b,l)\leftarrow\min\bigl(D_{i+1}(b,l),D_i(b_{\mathrm{old}},l_{\mathrm{old}})
+\mathrm{cost}_i(b)\bigr).
$$ {#eq-ch11-solids-dp}

`compute_min_flips` ({{< code src/bc/flip_zero_impl.h compute_min_flips >}}) implements @eq-ch11-solids-dp
with the cost rule of `can_flip` ({{< code src/bc/flip_zero_impl.h can_flip >}}) and records the predecessor
only on a strict improvement. The terminal run must also reach its minimum: the answer is the least cost
over the end states whose run length is at least $m_b$, and a line with no admissible end state returns
$-1$. Every admissible prefix ends in one of these states; induction on prefix length shows the recurrence
retains the smallest possible cost. `reconstruct_solution`
({{< code src/bc/flip_zero_impl.h reconstruct_solution >}}) walks the recorded predecessors back and writes
a minimizing line. This proves a line optimum, not a global multidimensional optimum after alternating
sweeps. `flip_zero_cpu` ({{< code src/bc/bc_dispatch.cpp flip_zero_cpu >}}) runs the two kernels on every
line of the tensor iterator with $m_0=3$, $m_1=2$ and only zero-to-one flips allowed, and sums the line
costs into an atomic counter. Check C5 compares an independent dynamic program with exhaustive enumeration
for every binary line of lengths two through eight.

For the partial implicit system, $\mathsf H=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1)$ on the density, normal momentum and
energy rows. A reflecting ghost increment is $\mathsf H\Delta\mathbf U_i$. Substitution into the lower
neighbour block contributes $\mathsf B_i\mathsf H\Delta\mathbf U_i$ to the diagonal; the upper side contributes
$\mathsf C_i\mathsf H\Delta\mathbf U_i$. Thus

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathsf A_i&\leftarrow\mathsf A_i+\mathsf B_i\mathsf H,\\
\mathsf A_i&\leftarrow\mathsf A_i+\mathsf C_i\mathsf H.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch11-solids-closure}

Apply each row only at its relevant fluid boundary. The vector `Bnd` of `vic_assemble_partial_impl`
({{< code src/implicit/vic_assemble_partial_impl.h vic_assemble_partial_impl >}}) implements
@eq-ch11-solids-closure: the lower row is added when the cell is the first of the column or `solid_lower`
is set, the upper row when it is the last or `solid_upper` is set. With `solid_lower` the same function also
mirrors the base state used in the lower face Jacobian, copying the cell's primitives to the solid side
with the normal velocity negated. A solid row has the identity divided by $\Delta t$ on the diagonal and
zero neighbour blocks (`setIdentity`, {{< code src/implicit/implicit_dispatch.cpp vic_assemble_partial_cpu >}}),
and its right-hand side is zeroed before the solve (`forward_masked`,
{{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_apply_implicit_correction >}}), so that row has a zero solved
increment. Check C6 verifies the block substitution algebra. The full-system closure
({{< code src/implicit/vic_assemble_full_impl.h vic_assemble_full_impl >}}) adds the same rows under an
additional non-periodic guard; this derivation does not assert an untested periodic-solid combination.
Checks C5 and C6 are [check `src/snapy_report/ch11/boundary_check.py`, output
`src/snapy_report/ch11/boundary_check.out`]; they do not call a snapy kernel.

### Numerical method

The mask has the three spatial extents of the block, ghosts included. `InternalBoundaryImpl::rectify_solid`
({{< code src/bc/rectify_solid.cpp InternalBoundaryImpl::rectify_solid >}}) makes it contiguous (which may
alias an already contiguous input), fills every ghost slab of every direction with more than one cell with
ones through the solid callbacks of @sec-ch11-custom, then sweeps x1, x2 and x3 in turn, alternating the
traversal direction, until a sweep makes no flip. Exhausting `max-iter` throws. The callbacks the caller
supplies are applied afterwards.

Initialization (`MeshBlockImpl::finalize_initialization`,
{{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::finalize_initialization >}}) saves separate primitive and
conserved fill states, equal to the initial state in solid cells with the velocity or momentum rows zeroed,
after `mark_prim_solid_` ({{< code src/bc/internal_boundary.cpp InternalBoundaryImpl::mark_prim_solid_ >}})
has written the placeholders into the primitives: the configured density and pressure, zero velocity and
zero composition. During a stage `HydroImpl::forward` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}})
marks the primitives again and passes the reconstructed face states of each direction through the interface
mirror; the time-step bound (`HydroImpl::max_time_step`, {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::max_time_step >}})
replaces the sound speed in solid cells by $10^{-8}\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. The implicit correction requires
both x1 faces physical, masks the solid increments and reads the placeholder primitives in solid cells.
After each RK combination `fill_cons_solid_`
({{< code src/bc/internal_boundary.cpp InternalBoundaryImpl::fill_cons_solid_ >}}) restores the conserved
fill state in solid cells, in `MeshBlockImpl::advance_local`
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}); only the hydro tensor is refilled. The
gravity-work fixer (`MeshBlockImpl::gravity_work_fixer_sums`,
{{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::gravity_work_fixer_sums >}}) zeroes the mass of solid cells
before it sums, so they take no share of the energy correction. The staircase geometry is cell-aligned, not a
cut-cell representation, and no geometric convergence order is measured.

: Implementation sites for solids. {#tbl-ch11-solids-code}

1. Read `max-iter` and the solid placeholders; require the mask shape at initialization. The anchor
   `max_iter` is in {{< code src/bc/internal_boundary.cpp InternalBoundaryOptionsImpl::from_yaml overload=2 >}}.
2. Mark the ghost slabs solid, run the directional minimum-flip sweeps, reject nonconvergence, then apply the
   optional mask callbacks. The anchor `rectify_solid` is in
   {{< code src/bc/rectify_solid.cpp InternalBoundaryImpl::rectify_solid >}}.
3. Save the fill states, mark the primitives, mirror the reconstructed interface states and mask the
   implicit system. The anchor `mark_prim_solid_` is in
   {{< code src/bc/internal_boundary.cpp InternalBoundaryImpl::mark_prim_solid_ >}}.
4. Refill the solid hydro cells after the stage combination and exclude the solids from the fixer's mass.
   The anchor `fill_cons_solid_` is in {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_rectify.release` | Every outer and inner ghost slab of a rectified mask is solid | exact equality | test fixture |
| `test_flip_zero_count.release` | The flip count on eight threads equals the serial count over twenty repeats | exact integer equality | test fixture |
| `test_implicit_stratified_solid_python` | A column with a solid segment or strided solids keeps the fluid mass of each segment and stays finite | mass error below $10^{-12}$ | script threshold |

: Source-defined assertions for solids; no runtime results. {#tbl-ch11-solids-tests}

The ghost-slab assertion is in `test2` ({{< code tests/test_rectify.cpp test2 >}}).

The thread comparison is the `serial` versus `parallel` count in `main`
({{< code tests/test_flip_zero_count.cpp main >}}).

The solid runs are built by `solid_run` ({{< code tests/test_implicit_stratified_solid.py solid_run >}}),
which reports the mass error of the fluid segments; the threshold is applied in the script's main block
({{< code tests/test_implicit_stratified_solid.py >}}).

Numeric tolerances above are the source test constants; a round-off derivation is not documented for each.
Device/rank distinctions and missing runs are recorded in @sec-ch15-ch11.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The per-line optimum does not make the multidimensional repaired mask globally minimal. The sweep loop
throws when its last permitted sweep still changes entries, even if one more sweep would have converged.
The mask and the fill states are static. The stage refill restores only the hydro tensor, not the passive
scalars ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}); scalar-solid isolation needs
runtime evidence. Diffusion coefficients at solid placeholders need a separate analysis; no quantitative
placeholder contamination measurement is reused here. An x1 decomposition with the implicit solve is
rejected ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_apply_implicit_correction >}}).

Untested switch combinations remain subject to @sec-ch12-matrix. No new CPU, CUDA or multi-rank solver result
is claimed.
:::
